top_categories.workout_context: 69ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Atlas Gran Fondo's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before November.
At Atlas Gran Fondo, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.

Road-specific control matters at Atlas Gran Fondo. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 99 miles.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Atlas Gran Fondo. Train it until it feels boring.
6,889ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
At mile 60 of 99, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
6,889ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 99 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Two threshold sessions per week without the recovery cost of VO2max work. For 99 miles, sustainable FTP gains matter more than peak power.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 6,889ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
Low-cadence force work supports 6,889ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.

race_overlay.weather: November in Taroudant, Morocco. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks before Atlas Gran Fondo. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Atlas Gran Fondo’s 99 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at Atlas Gran Fondo. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Atlas Gran Fondo rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on TT Threshold, Race Simulation, and Over Under to prepare you for 99 miles of mixed terrain in Taroudant, Morocco.
